items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Duke Ellington, Ike Dixon a band from Baltimore, Maryland. Charlie Johnson...

ctx.x: Looking back, I realize now that that kind of parade music was a basis for Jazz. That was how many Jazz players learned the harmonic connections. The rhythm came from the Churches. When I was about twelve years old, there used to be meetings of the "Holy Rollies", In the yard of a big house right on the corner near where we lived. They used to clap their hands, and the preacher was a wonderful tap dancer. He could really whip up the congregation with his rhythm. My mother was a Baptist, and we were all made to go…

I was going to school on 9th Street which was near where I lived and I had a playmate who was blond and Irish. In Kentucky the white and negro children never played together. But that was not the case in Cincinnati because the schools were mixed at that time. This boy lived near me on 9th Street and his mother worked in a laundry a few blocks up from the school and she used to give us pennies now and then to buy candy. We used to fight with two Jewish boys who were twins and whose names I remember being Ike and…

Cincinnati was like New Orleans in many ways because the same boats that sailed up and down the Ohio river from New Orleans to Kansas City all stopped in Cincinnati which also had a levee. The ways and means of making a living in certain parts of Cincinnati from the levee up to certain streets was exactly like New Orleans, because there were saloons, gambling and prostitutes. The streets where the exciment took place were George Street from Mound to Central Avenue, 6th Street from Mound to John Street, Carlisle…
